description: A small solar-powered car, built and running. Anton Pechenko's project: 3D models, print-ready STL files, CadQuery source code and an assembly guide. Open source under MIT.
ogDescription: From an idea to a working car. Print the parts, put them together and build your own.

designIntro: The solar panels power the motor. Gears turn the axle, and the wheels move the car. The printed structure holds everything together.
designAlt: Chassis and two empty panel frames, showing the eight straight support posts
designCaption: The chassis, posts and frames are 3D-printed parts.
panelsText: The front panel tilts by 20° and the rear by 10°. The rear panel's center sits 15 mm higher.
motorText: The cradle is part of the chassis. A cable tie secures the motor, and printed test pieces helped us choose the gear center distance.
framesText: Eight straight posts connect the chassis to the frames. Fasteners are built into both ends of each post — no separate screws or wedges.
buildEyebrow: From a model to a real object
buildTitle:
Piece by piece.
Then into the sun.
buildIntro: The exploded view shows the released V2.10 chassis and BF5 mounts. Build the drivetrain first, attach the empty frames, and install the panels last.
step1Text: One chassis, two frames and eight posts. Choose orientation and supports in your slicer; the STL files contain no built-in supports.
step2Text: Install the axles, wheels and gears. Place the motor in its cradle and secure it with a cable tie.
step3Text: Insert the posts into the empty frames from below. Engage the chassis snaps one at a time, pressing near each post. Route the wires and fit the panels last.
step4Text: Check that the wheels turn freely and let the car run. The most rewarding part of the project.
printer: Printed on a Creality Ender 3 S1

hardwareText: For the purchased components, see “Where to get the hardware” above. This build uses two donor kits for their two panels, plus one motor, four wheels, two axles, gears, wires and a cable tie.
layoutsText: The archive also includes combined frame and post layouts. Choose either the layouts or the individual parts to avoid printing duplicates. All dimensions are in millimeters; print at 100% scale.
releaseNote: Chassis V2.10 · Panel mounts BF5 · The builder has confirmed that the assembled car works. Fit depends on your printer and hardware.

hardwareIntro: The working car was built using parts from two SICWUD wooden solar-car kits from Temu. Only this two-kit build has been tested.
kitAlt: Product photo of the SICWUD wooden solar car kit, with one panel, motor and four wheels
kitPhotoCredit: Product photo from the linked Temu listing; rights belong to its owner.
kitText: Each kit has one solar panel; our car uses two. Take both panels, plus one motor, four wheels, two axles and a matched gear pair. The other drivetrain is spare.
kitVariant: Choose the “Solar car” variant. The wooden chassis is replaced by the printed V2.10 chassis and BF5 mounts.
kitNote: The builder supplied this exact product link. Listings and shipping options can vary by country.
separateIntro: The links below are candidates for sourcing alternatives. Their compatibility as a complete car has not been verified. Check the dimensions and electrical compatibility before ordering.
motorAlternative: The seller’s drawing shows Ø24.3 × 12.4 mm, with 6.2 mm of exposed shaft. Slightly larger than our measured Ø24 × 12 mm motor. Check cradle fit, pinion fit, gear alignment and operation with your panels. Sold without a gear.
wheelAlternative: Listed as Ø30 × 10 mm wheels for a 2 mm axle. The pack contains 8 wheels and 4 steel Ø2 × 100 mm axles. Use four wheels and two axles; cut the axles to fit the car.
panelAlternative: Listed as 55 × 55 mm, 2 V panels with wires. Thickness is not specified; our frames require 2 mm panels. Confirm thickness, inactive border and motor compatibility. Sold by MSL Solar Company Store.
hardwareRest: The gear pair is selected by nominal dimensions, not a physical fit test. The seller does not specify a usable pressure angle; confirm the tooth profiles match and check shaft grip and free meshing. The original large gear’s tooth count is still unconfirmed. The donor kit’s gears remain the tested option. Also allow for wires and a 4 mm cable tie.
explodedAlt: Exploded solar car: panels above frames, eight labeled posts beneath the frames, chassis with axles and separated wheels, and the motor beside its cradle
legend1Text: The motor cradle and axle supports are already part of the base.
legend2Text: Four wheels on two Ø2 mm axles. Put the large gear on the rear axle.
legend3Text: Seat the motor in the cradle, align the gears and secure it with a 4 mm cable tie.
legend4Text: Two of each: F1, F2, R1 and R2. F = front frame, R = rear frame. Type 1 goes at the rear edge; type 2 at the front edge.
legend5Text: Insert posts from below, with the upper latch tongues facing the central opening. Then snap the lower ends into the chassis.
legend6Text: Route the wires through the frame openings. Fit the panels only after all posts are locked in place.
diagramNote: Printed parts use the released CAD geometry. Purchased parts are simplified; gear teeth, wires and the cable tie are omitted. The view explains mechanical assembly, not electrical wiring.
gearTitle: Gears for the motor and rear axle
gearIntro: A candidate pair from Pinion Parts Store on AliExpress: 10 and 50 teeth, both module 0.5. For standard spur gears this gives a nominal 15 mm center distance and a 5:1 reduction, matching our chassis spacing. This pair has not been tested in the car.
pinionDescription: Choose “10 Teeth” and “2mm Tight”. The seller’s drawing shows Ø5.97 mm, 9.2 mm long and a 1.96 mm bore for a press fit on a 2 mm shaft. Confirm the replacement motor’s shaft diameter and align the pinion with the axle gear.
axleGearDescription: Choose “50 Teeth” and “2mm Tight”. The seller’s drawing shows Ø26 mm, a 1.6 mm tooth face, 4.4 mm total width and a 1.95 mm bore for a press fit on the 2 mm axle. Check hub clearance and tooth alignment.
separateStatus: A build using separately purchased components has not been tested.
